goal: Review the code in https://github.com/karpathy/micrograd for bugs, correctness and design problems. Produce a prioritized list with evidence.

plan.reason: The goal is a code review of a small, fully listed Python codebase (engine.py, nn.py, tests, setup.py, README) which can be done by reading the sandbox files.

subtasks.title: Review engine.py for correctness and bugs
subtasks.instructions: Read repos/karpathy__micrograd/micrograd/engine.py. Analyze the Value class and its __add__, __mul__, __truediv__, __pow__, __neg__, __lt__, __le__, __gt__, __ge__, __repr__, backward(), and _backward methods for correctness, edge cases, and design problems. Specifically check: (1) the __truediv__ implementation (does it correctly handle the case where self is a constant and other is a Value, or vice versa?); (2) the __pow__ implementation (does it correctly handle the case where self is a constant and other is a Value, or vice versa?); (3) the backward() method (does it correctly handle the case where the graph is not a DAG, or where there are multiple paths to a node?); (4) the _backward methods for each operation (are the gradients correct?); (5) any potential division by zero or other numerical issues. Quote specific lines as evidence for each finding.

subtasks.title: Review nn.py and tests for correctness and coverage
subtasks.instructions: Read repos/karpathy__micrograd/micrograd/nn.py and repos/karpathy__micrograd/test/test_engine.py. For nn.py, analyze the Linear class and its forward and backward passes for correctness. Check: (1) does the Linear class correctly compute the forward pass (y = x @ w.T + b)?; (2) does it correctly compute the backward pass (gradients for x, w, b)?; (3) are there any issues with the initialization of parameters? For test_engine.py, analyze the test cases for coverage and correctness. Check: (1) do the tests cover all operations in engine.py?; (2) do the tests check both forward and backward passes?; (3) are there any missing edge cases (e.g., division by zero, negative exponents)? Quote specific lines as evidence for each finding.

subtasks.title: Review setup.py, README, and notebooks for design and documentation issues
subtasks.instructions: Read repos/karpathy__micrograd/setup.py, repos/karpathy__micrograd/README.md, repos/karpathy__micrograd/demo.ipynb, and repos/karpathy__micrograd/trace_graph.ipynb. Analyze for design and documentation problems. For setup.py, check: (1) are the package dependencies correctly specified?; (2) is the package structure correct? For README.md, check: (1) does it accurately describe the library's capabilities?; (2) are there any misleading or incorrect statements? For the notebooks, check: (1) do they demonstrate the library correctly?; (2) are there any errors or inconsistencies in the examples? Quote specific lines or cells as evidence for each finding.

s1.title: Review engine.py for correctness and bugs

findings.title: __pow__ rejects Value exponents via assert
findings.detail: Line 36 asserts other is int/float, so Value**Value raises AssertionError instead of computing a gradient; __truediv__ (line 88) works only because -1 is a literal int, not a Value.

evidence.quote: assert isinstance(other, (int, float)), "only supporting int/float powers for now"

findings.title: backward() assumes a DAG; no cycle or multi-path guard
findings.detail: build_topo uses a visited set so a cyclic graph silently drops edges, and gradients are accumulated with += (lines 18-19, 29-30) so multiple paths to a node are summed, but there is no explicit topological-order validation or cycle detection.

findings.title: __pow__ numerical edge case at data=0 with negative exponent
findings.detail: self.data**other with other negative and self.data==0 raises ZeroDivisionError; the _backward also computes self.data**(other-1) which is undefined at 0 for non-positive exponents.

findings.title: __truediv__ relies on __pow__ with literal -1
findings.detail: __truediv__ (line 88) and __rtruediv__ (line 91) delegate to __pow__ with -1, which passes the int/float assert, so division works, but the gradient path is indirect and inherits __pow__'s limitations.

findings.title: grad not reset before backward; stale gradients accumulate
findings.detail: backward() sets self.grad=1 but does not reset grad to 0 for all other nodes in the graph, so calling backward() twice on the same graph accumulates stale gradients via += in _backward closures.

s1.summary: Reviewed engine.py; found a real bug in __pow__ (assertion blocks Value**Value), a design flaw in backward() (no DAG/multi-path handling, relies on +=), and a numerical edge case in __pow__ at data=0 with negative exponent.
s1.feedback: Findings are accurate and well-supported by the file. The __pow__ assert (line 36) correctly identified as blocking Value exponents; backward() DAG assumption and += accumulation (lines 58-70) correctly noted; numerical edge case at data=0 with negative exponent (line 40) is valid; __truediv__ delegation to __pow__ with -1 (line 88) is correctly described; stale gradient accumulation on repeated backward() calls (line 68) is a real issue. All evidence quotes verified. No off-topic or exaggerated claims.

s2.title: Review nn.py and tests for correctness and coverage

findings.title: No Linear class in nn.py
findings.detail: nn.py defines Neuron, Layer, MLP instead of a Linear class; forward is y = sum(wi*xi)+b, equivalent to x@w.T+b.

evidence.quote: act = sum((wi*xi for wi,xi in zip(self.w, x)), self.b)

findings.title: Weight init unnormalized
findings.detail: Weights drawn from uniform(-1,1) without scaling by fan-in (e.g. 1/sqrt(nin)), which can cause large activations/gradients for wide layers.

findings.title: Tests do not cover nn.py
findings.detail: test_engine.py only imports Value from engine; no tests exercise Neuron, Layer, MLP forward/backward, so nn.py correctness is unverified.

findings.title: Missing edge cases in tests
findings.detail: No tests for division by zero, negative exponents, or relu at zero; engine __truediv__ and __pow__ can produce inf/nan or assert failures untested.

evidence.quote: assert isinstance(other, (int, float)), "only supporting int/float powers for now"

findings.title: Backward pass correctness relies on engine
findings.detail: nn.py has no explicit backward; gradients flow through Value ops. Correct only if engine ops are correct, which tests do verify for engine but not for nn modules.

s3.title: Review setup.py, README, and notebooks for design and documentation issues

findings.title: setup.py declares no dependencies
findings.detail: setup.py has no install_requires, which is correct since micrograd has no third-party deps, but trace_graph.ipynb requires graphviz without documenting it in setup.py extras.

findings.title: trace_graph.ipynb uses private API _prev and _op
findings.detail: The notebook accesses Value._prev and Value._op directly, coupling documentation to internal implementation details that could break without notice.

findings.title: trace_graph.ipynb render call lacks extension
findings.detail: dot.render('gout') relies on graphviz default extension; the repo ships gout.svg, implying SVG output, but the code does not specify format explicitly in render.

findings.title: setup.py missing install_requires for PyTorch used by tests
findings.detail: Tests require PyTorch as a reference, but setup.py declares no dependencies at all, so users must know to install it manually.

evidence.quote: To run the unit tests you will have to install [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/), which the tests use as a reference for verifying the correctness of the calculated gradients.

findings.title: README references puppy.jpg image not present in repo
findings.detail: README embeds an image puppy.jpg that does not exist in the repository file listing, so the image will not render.

findings.title: README references moon_mlp.png not present in repo
findings.detail: README embeds moon_mlp.png which is not in the file listing, so the decision boundary image will not render.

findings.title: README example uses in-place += on Value objects
findings.detail: The example mutates Values with += (e.g. c += c + 1), which is an unusual and potentially confusing API for an autograd engine and may not be intended for users.

findings.title: README microgpt explainer post date appears in the future
findings.detail: The README links to an explainer post dated 2026-02-12, which is a future date and likely a typo.

evidence.quote: See also the accompanying [explainer post](https://karpathy.github.io/2026/02/12/microgpt/) for a detailed walkthrough.
